references.text: The original instruction to gather onyx stones and setting stones for the ephod and breastplate, repeated in 35:9.
Describes the use of the onyx stones on the shoulder pieces of the ephod, with the names of the sons of Israel engraved upon them.
A detailed description of the twelve setting stones to be placed on the breastplate (hoshen).
Description of the ephod for which the onyx stones and setting stones were to be used.
Description of the breastplate (hoshen) and its stones mentioned in the verse.
The execution of the work with the onyx stones for the ephod, fulfilling the instruction in 35:9.
The execution of the work with the setting stones for the breastplate, fulfilling the instruction in 35:9.
The first mention of the onyx stone (shoham) in the Bible, in the description of the land of Havilah.
Mentions the onyx stone among precious gems, showing the stone's value in biblical times.
David gathered onyx stones and setting stones for the temple, reflecting the materials of the tabernacle.
Highlights the special contribution and responsibility of the leaders (chiefs) in delivering the most valuable stones.
